facts.statement: Fossils of Emausaurus were found in the Lehmhagen Member in northern Germany.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Lehmhagen Member, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, northern Germany.

facts.statement: Emausaurus is the only known armored dinosaur from the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Emausaurus is the only known Toarcian thyreophoran, as well as the only dinosaur from the zone of the same age with a formal name.

facts.statement: The species Emausaurus ernsti was named and described by Hartmut Haubold in 1990.
facts.quote: The type and only species, E. ernsti, was named and described by Hartmut Haubold in 1990.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes parts of the skull, jaw, vertebrae, limbs, and armor plates.
facts.quote: It is known by the right side of the skull, the right lower jaw, caudal vertebrae, neural arches, a radius, a metatarsal, a claw, fragments of ribs, scutes, and plates, known as EMAU SGWG 85.

facts.statement: Emausaurus was likely covered in body armor made of osteoderms.
facts.quote: Emausaurus was probably a semi-bipedal to quadrupedal animal, being covered in an armor of osteoderms across the body.

facts.statement: Emausaurus was likely a low-browsing herbivore that ate cycads and Bennettitales.
facts.quote: Like other thyreophorans, it probably was an herbivore, specifically a low dwelling one, with a diet associated with ground flora, such as cycads and Bennettitales.

facts.statement: The juvenile holotype of Emausaurus was estimated to be 2 to 2.5 meters long and weigh between 50 and 90 kilograms.
facts.quote: The body length of the holotype juvenile individual of Emausaurus has been estimated at 2 - 2.5 m, with a body mass of 50 – 90 kg.

facts.statement: Adult Emausaurus are estimated to have reached lengths of 3 to 4 meters and weights up to 240 kilograms.
facts.quote: The adult length has been estimated at 3 - 4 m, with a body mass up to 240 kg.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses place Emausaurus as a basal member of the Thyreophora, between Scutellosaurus and Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: Cladistic analyses have shown that Emausaurus was a basal member of the Thyreophora, more derived than Scutellosaurus, but less than Scelidosaurus.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic position of Emausaurus is controversial because the known specimen is immature.
facts.quote: The cladistic status of the specimen is relatively controversial due to its young nature.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Emausaurus is more derived than Scelidosaurus or a sister taxon to Stegosauria.
facts.quote: Emausaurus may be more derived than Scelidosaurus, or even be a sister taxon to Stegosauria.

facts.statement: Emausaurus possessed a sinuous jaw profile, a feature more advanced than that of the basal genus Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: Emausaurus has a sinuous jaw profile, more advanced in ankylosauromorphs, unlike the rectilinear morphology seen in the more basal genus Scutellosaurus.

facts.statement: Although few osteoderms have been found, they indicate Emausaurus was covered in armor, though the extent of coverage is unknown.
facts.quote: The animal was covered in osteoderms, although the few found give no indication of how extensively they were distributed across the torso.

facts.statement: Emausaurus forelimbs were adapted for weight support rather than grasping, with conical, slightly curved claws.
facts.quote: The forelimb shows adaptations for weight support, rather than grasping, having ungual phalanges that are conical and only slightly decurved.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Emausaurus was a quadrupedal, low-roaming herbivore adapted for supporting its weight.
facts.quote: A series of characters that together are suggestive of graviportality and quadrupedality, making Emausaurus a low roaming herbivore.

facts.statement: Later studies criticize assumptions of bipedality or quadrupedality in Emausaurus due to its incomplete nature and close relationship with Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: Later works however have criticised this assumption given the relationships with Scutellosaurus are more likely and recommend to not infer bipedality or quadrupedality as the taxon is incomplete.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in a Lower Toarcian shale layer at the Emausaurus type site.
facts.quote: The holotype of Emausaurus was found in the so-called "Emausaurus type site", which represents a shale ingression from the Lehmhagen Member, dated from the Lower Toarcian.

facts.statement: The fossil site contains invertebrates including insects, bivalves, sea snails, and ammonites.
facts.quote: The invertebrate fauna consists of insects, bivalves, sea snails and ammonites (Tiltoniceras, Eleganticeras and Lobolytoceras).

facts.statement: Fish fossils from the site include the genera Saurorhynchus, Grimmenichthys, and Grimmenodon.
facts.quote: The vertebrate fauna is also diverse, with fossils of the fish genera Saurorhynchus, Grimmenichthys, and Grimmenodon.

facts.statement: Emausaurus lived approximately 185 million years ago during the Early Jurassic Toarcian in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios de periodo Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 185 millones de años, en el Toarciano, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: An adult Emausaurus was a small armored dinosaur measuring 4 meters long, 0.70 meters high, and weighing 30 kilograms.
facts.quote: Un Emausaurus adulto era un pequeño dinosaurio acorazado, que media 4 metros de largo y 0,70 de alto con un peso de 30 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The holotype of Emausaurus was estimated to be around 2 meters long, but represented a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: La longitud corporal del holotipo de Emausaurus se ha estimado en alrededor de 2 metros sin embargo representó a un individuo juvenil.

facts.statement: Its small head ended in a horny beak with leaf-shaped teeth that allowed it to strip buds and low plants.
facts.quote: La pequeña cabeza terminaba en un pico córneo, con dientes en forma de hoja, que le permitían desgajar los brotes y plantas bajas.

facts.statement: Like Scelidosaurus, it had protective armor consisting of a very hard skin riveted with strong, round scales.
facts.quote: Como el Scelidosaurus, tenía una armadura protectora, una piel muy dura remachada con escamas redondas y fuertes.

facts.statement: The armor included three conical shields and a tall, spiny element.
facts.quote: La armadura incluye tres escudos cónicos y un elemento alto y espinoso.

facts.statement: When walking, it kept its tail held upright.
facts.quote: Cuando caminaba mantenía la cola erguida.

facts.statement: Emausaurus was found in Germany in Bituminous Shale in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
facts.quote: Emausaurus se encontró en Alemania en Bituminosen Schiefer, Mecklenberg-Vorpommern.

facts.statement: The type species, Emausaurus ernsti, was formally described by Haubold in 1991.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Emausaurus ernsti, fue formalizado por Haubold en 1991.

facts.statement: The specific name is also in honor of the Ernst Moritz Arndt University.
facts.quote: El nombre específico también es en honor a la universidad.

facts.statement: The specific name derives from geologist Werner Ernst, who found the holotype fossil SGWG 85 in the summer of 1963 near a lake in Grimmen within Toarcian strata.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se deriva del nombre del geólogo Werner Ernst, quien encontró el fósil, holotipo SGWG 85, en el verano de 1963 en un lago cerca de Grimmen, en estratos que datan del Toarciano.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses showed that Emausaurus was a basal member of Thyreophora, more derived than Scutellosaurus but less derived than Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: Los análisis cladístico mostraron que Emausaurus era un miembro basal de Thyreophora, más derivado que Scutellosaurus, pero menos que Scelidosaurus.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Scelidosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Scelidosauridae

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Scelidosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Scelidosauridae

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: It lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)
